Record date: 2126-08-14
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 78 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 08/14/26 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of bilateral lower extremity edema, reassessment of fatigue, and monitoring of anxiety and depressive symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for his follow-up appointment one month after his last visit. He reports a slight improvement in his dyspnea but continues to experience significant limitations during physical activity, particularly during ambulation. He notes that he has been using his albuterol inhaler approximately six to eight times daily, which is a reduction from his previous usage, likely due to increased adherence to his inhaled corticosteroids.
Despite the reduction in albuterol usage, Mr. Fairfaxs bilateral lower extremity edema remains persistent. He continues to follow a low-sodium diet and is compliant with his furosemide regimen, which has been adjusted to 100 mg daily in light of the nephrology consultation recommendations. He describes the edema as still being 1+ pitting but reports that it has not worsened since the last visit.
Mr. Fairfax indicates that his fatigue persists and is still debilitating, although he has noticed some improvement in his mood since increasing his therapy sessions with a psychologist. He reports feeling slightly less anxious and depressed, attributing this to both medication and the support he has received.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + persistent fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + daytime dyspnea, + nocturnal wheezing, - cough, - sputum production, no hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain in knees and hands, no swelling. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, reduced use to six to eight times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 1 puff twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 1 puff daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 100 mg daily (increased per nephrology's recommendation). 7. Sertraline 50 mg daily (ongoing management for anxiety and depression).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 78, BP 126/76, RR 22, O2 sat 85% on room air
General: Elderly male in no acute distress but appears fatigued and mildly anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, mild wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 1+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.5, Hgb 11.0, Hct 33.0, Plt 210 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.2, Cl 96, CO2 22, BUN 30, Cr 1.5, Glucose 88 3. BNP: 600 (notable decrease). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.5 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's dyspnea has shown slight improvement, and his inhaler technique continues to be reinforced. He is encouraged to remain compliant with his inhaled corticosteroids and to continue pulmonary rehabilitation. Follow-up in 1 month for reassessment. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. Blood pressure remains stable. Follow-up in 1 month. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent edema has improved slightly with the increase in furosemide. Reinforcement of dietary sodium restrictions is advised, and Mr. Fairfax is encouraged to continue leg elevation. A follow-up with nephrology is recommended. 4. Fatigue and psychological well-being: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily. Mr. Fairfax has reported improvements in anxiety and depressive symptoms, and ongoing psychological support is encouraged. Monitor CBC and metabolic panel in one month to assess for any changes.
Patient education reiterated regarding recognizing signs of exacerbation, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
